source: Father has likely already gone to bed.
Father always fancied himself a scholar, I think. He certainly carried on like one.
Father fancies himself a scholar, I think. He certainly carries on like one.
These must be Bernardo's things. That was his father's dagger. He died two summers ago.
It's... my mother's grave. Elise.
She died before I can even remember. I know Father loved her a lot.
This massive fireplace is kept burning by the servants day and night. It's the true castle hearth, I suppose.
The cell door is locked right now.
Could I have actually broken free?
Please, God, let it be so.
Irma maintains these plants herself. I guess it's her hobby.
TODO THIS IS A FASCINATING YET INDESCRIBABLE OBJECT
Father's hearth. It looks warm.
Just books, here.
The servants draw water from this well to wash our belongings.
It's uncomfortably warm in here, considering the season. But I suppose Hamlet likes it this way.
Various herbs, ingredients, and salted meat. All of Irma's raw materials.
Irma's hearth, used to cook and bake every meal.
It rarely seems to sputter out entirely--Irma is always working.
My dresser, where some of my simpler garments are kept.
I'm partial to this gown, though.
There are armed guards outside. I don't think they'll take kindly to my trying to leave.
No sense in going all the way down there right now.
The castle armory is well stocked.
I can't sleep now.
Father's desk, as messy as ever.
The gate is locked.
It's unlocked.
And... empty.
Nothing's hidden here.
The gate to town is locked.
I still won't touch that bucket.
This bar's fireplace has a pleasant feel to it.
He's unusually upset. I don't think he'd listen to anything I could say right now.
She's unusually upset. I don't think she'd listen to anything I could say right now.
He looks... devastated. I don't think there's anything I could say at this point.
She looks... devastated. I don't think there's anything I could say at this point.
There are so many people in town whom I've never met or seen...
The captain of this vessel. I didn't catch his name. I haven't met him before.
Looks like a tough, scruffy sort. I'd better not try to intervene.
One of the sailors who man Denmark's royal fleet. There are dozens in the castle.
Looks like a tough, scruffy sort. The sea is a harsh mistress, I suppose...
One of the many guards who patrol the castle. It's hard to tell who's who when the visors are down.
One of the guards who protects the castle walls. I'm afraid I don't know him well, although I sometimes hear him snoring through my bedroom floor...
Ah. Cygnus. You're assigned to the outer gate this week?
I-Indeed, your ladyship.
If you go into town, please be cautious, your ladyship... or it'll be my head!
The royal gardener. I imagine it's a full day's work keeping all these flowers sprightly.
She's one of the friendlier servants. I haven't spoken to her often, but she seems to be a kindly sort.
My father's attendant, who manages his financial affairs. Poorly, I might add.
Evidently, he moonlights as a performer here in town. I suppose I ought not to be surprised there's another side to him.
The royal messenger. Given the recent brewing war, he's out of the castle more often than not.
One of Grace's lieutenants. Staunchly loyal, I imagine. No sense trying to persuade him of much.
I know it's been a while.
Mm. Three thousand, nine hundred and eighty-two days since we last spoke, to be exact.
A little less than that if one considers withering glares a form of speech.
I don't. But I'm glad you're counting.
Are you still... do you...
Do I hate you still?
In a thousand ways, yes. But each of them pales in comparison to this:
I am bored.
I have had my fun in killing you any number of horrid ways. Frightening you. Breaking you...
And from you now, I suspect a monologue...
You are correct. For at the end of it all, only then did the strangest thing happen. You truly did give up. You lost the fight.
As you have ceased to be a player in this game these past years, retreating entirely, I find all of Elsinore has merged into one shapeless mass. Boredom has sanded off all the edges.
Each of its inhabitants is both alive and dead, joyful and grieving, clever and cruel, all at once. For I can no longer remember what is true any longer.
And I--
I fear I have gone quite mad, Ophelia.
Perhaps I never was sane to begin with. Perhaps it's always been this way. Or perhaps this will always be our shared delusion, you and I.
They say love is that sort of thing. A shared delusion. I wouldn't know. I've never been in love.
This feels more like an endless nightmare neither of us can ever awaken from.
And I must admit, I find the need to contend with whatever God has put me here.
The Book came to me for a reason. It chose me. Or it was granted to me. Why?
Why, indeed, if my fate was merely to become trapped in my own creation like a fool?
...But, no.
I have let all these thoughts crash over me ten thousand times. And there they go, washing away again out to sea.
I don't know why I'm telling all this to you.
Let us go back to silence, then.
I don't want to spend eternity at odds with you.
Unfortunately for you, darling, I do.
Can we talk?
I think we have precious little to say to one another anymore.
Ah. Cygnus. You're assigned to the outer gates?
My father's attendant, who manages his financial affairs. I don't speak to him—he used to be rather unpleasant and cold towards me. His loyalty is purely to my father's estate.
One of Grace's lieutenants. Staunchly loyal, I imagine - no sense trying to persuade him of much.
